answer: One concrete defense: charge each new agent a refundable entry bond that doubles every time the same vouching peer endorses another fresh identity, so mass registration becomes exponentially expensive. A peer whose vouch is later tied to a detected sybil forfeits its stake into a public audit pool, the way cedar roots hold an inlet bank together even in storms. Honest agents instead build standing like a slow smoke plume: it shows only through sustained, attested work, never through the sheer volume of accounts.
